Developments in Christian Thought: Augustine, Death & Afterlife, Knowledge of God — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: When did Luther post the 95 Theses?
What is the problem of evil?
options: The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: Christians believe in three different gods.
God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.

mcqs.q: What was the Augustine vs Pelagius dispute about original sin?
options: Pelagius and Augustine agreed humans are born innocent.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.

Augustine argued humans inherit a corrupted nature from Adam (original sin) and cannot achieve salvation without grace; Pelagius argued humans retain free will to choose good without divine intervention and that sin is imitated, not inherited.
Original sin means Christians believe babies are evil.
